layers.note: The dominant canopy tree of lowland western Washington; its young trees come up in openings far more than under closed canopy.

moisture.note: Grows from dry to moist ground and dominates well-drained sites; it tolerates saturated or flooded soil poorly, so it drops out on wet ground near water.

heat_load.note: Grows on every aspect and tolerates warm, dry south- and west-facing slopes better than western redcedar or bigleaf maple; only the coolest steep north-east slopes thin it.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in the Olympic Mountains and the west Cascades, where true firs and mountain hemlock take over.

max_slope_deg.note: Roots on steep slopes and rocky ground; thins out on the steepest.

shade_tolerance.note: Intermediate to intolerant of shade near the coast: seedlings need gaps or open ground.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −9 °C, gone by −14 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12.5 to 24 °C; gone below 10 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.4, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in western Washington lowland forests; not yet checked against Silvics of North America (Burns and Honkala, 1990) or the Fire Effects Information System, both public-domain USDA Forest Service works. Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Douglas-fir grows from central British Columbia to central California on the coast and through the Rockies to Mexico inland; its coastal variety in the mild, humid lowlands (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
